Yes, the limit holds. In fact, both the series and the integral tend to \(0\).

Assume \(c\ge 1\). For any \(t>0\), by AM-GM,
\[
t+\frac{c}{t}\ge 2\sqrt c.
\]

### Integral
Let
\[
I(c)=\int_1^\infty c e^{-x-\frac{c}{x}}\,dx.
\]
Split at \(R=2\sqrt c\). For \(1\le x\le R\),
\[
c e^{-x-\frac{c}{x}}\le c e^{-2\sqrt c}.
\]
For \(x\ge R\), since \(e^{-c/x}\le 1\),
\[
c e^{-x-\frac{c}{x}}\le c e^{-x}.
\]
Thus
\[
I(c)\le (R-1)c e^{-2\sqrt c}+\int_R^\infty c e^{-x}\,dx
\le 2c^{3/2}e^{-2\sqrt c}+c e^{-2\sqrt c}.
\]
Since \(e^{2\sqrt c}\) dominates any power of \(c\),
\[
I(c)\to 0.
\]

### Series
Let
\[
S(c)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty c e^{-n-\frac{c}{n}}
\]
and choose \(m=\lceil 2\sqrt c\rceil\). Then for \(n\le m\),
\[
c e^{-n-\frac{c}{n}}\le c e^{-2\sqrt c},
\]
while for \(n>m\),
\[
c e^{-n-\frac{c}{n}}\le c e^{-n}.
\]
Hence
\[
S(c)\le m c e^{-2\sqrt c}+c\sum_{n>m}e^{-n}
\le (2\sqrt c+1)c e^{-2\sqrt c}+\frac{c}{1-e^{-1}}e^{-2\sqrt c}\to 0.
\]

Therefore the asserted limit holds, and the common value is

\[
\boxed{0}
\]
